text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said an increase of some five percent in energy prices could be expected next year but would affect only corporate clients, not private citizens.
- Unemployment is expected to fall to 11.3 percent next year, from the current 12.2 percent, Kozlik said.

- Klaus Naumann, chairman of the NATO military committee, refuted speculation that Slovakia would not be among the the first wave of candidates for NATO. So far no official decision has been taken on which country, and when, would be accepted in the alliance, he said.
- The opposition Democratic Union (DU) accused the ruling coalition in Slovakia of being "more arrogant and aggressive" than the previous communist regime.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's imports of electric energy next year are expected to account for some 20 percent of the country's annual consumption, the monopoly energy utility Slovenske Elektrarne said.
- Overall retail sales totalled 279.7 billion crowns for the whole of 1995, compared with 233.8 billion in 1994.
- Textile and clothing company Makyta said it planned to invest 80 million crowns this year, mainly in modernising technology.

- Building society PSS, a joint-venture of the largest Slovak savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna, Germany's Bausparkasse Schwaebisch Hall and Austria's Raiffeisen Bausparkasse Wien, said it had signed 800,000 contracts during the first four years of its activities in Slovakia.
SME - President Michal Kovac rejected accusations by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar that he had informed journalists about Meciar's alleged serious illness.
